name: IS62C256AL-45ULI-TR
title: IS62C256AL / IS65C256AL: 32K × 8 low-power CMOS static RAM, 5 V
summary: A 256 Kbit asynchronous static RAM organised as 32,768 words by 8 bits, running from a single 5 V ± 10 % supply with TTL-level inputs and outputs. Fifteen address lines, eight data lines and three active-low controls (CE, OE, WE) make up the interface; with CE high and inputs at CMOS levels it draws 5 µA typical, and it keeps its data with VDD down to 2.0 V. It comes in 25 ns and 45 ns grades for commercial, industrial (IS62C256AL) and automotive (IS65C256AL) temperatures, in 28-pin SOP or TSOP type I. IS62C256AL-45ULI is the 45 ns industrial part in lead-free plastic SOP.

circuits.description: Output load for the timing measurements: the output pin is pulled to 5 V through 480 Ω and to ground through 255 Ω, with 5 pF from the pin to ground standing for the jig and scope. It is the load for the output turn-on and turn-off times (tLZOE, tHZOE, tLZCS, tHZCS).

operation.text: Asynchronous static RAM of 32,768 bytes (32K × 8, 262,144 bits) in CMOS. It needs no clock and no refresh; inputs and outputs are TTL-level, and it runs from one 5 V supply. Pinout matches other 32K × 8 SRAMs in plastic SOP and TSOP type I.
With CE high the chip is deselected and drops into standby; with inputs held at CMOS levels the typical standby dissipation is 150 µW. Typical active dissipation is 200 mW.
Active-low CE and OE let several devices share an address and data bus; WE selects between writing and reading.

Reads take place with WE high. With CE and OE held low, data follows the address: new data appears tAA after an address change and the old data stays valid for tOHA. When the read is started by CE or OE, the outputs leave high impedance after tLZCS or tLZOE, data is valid tACS after CE falls and tDOE after OE falls, and the outputs float again tHZCS or tHZOE after either returns high. For a CE-started read the address is valid no later than the falling edge of CE.

Three write timings are given: CE-controlled (OE high or low), WE-controlled with OE high, and WE-controlled with OE low. A write lasts while CE and WE are both low and ends on whichever rises first; address setup tSA is counted to the start, tAW and tSCS to the end, and data must be valid tSD before and tHD after the end. While WE is low the outputs go to high impedance after tHZWE and return tLZWE after it rises. With OE high the data lines stay at high impedance throughout.

Contents are kept with VDD down to VDR = 2.0 V provided CE is held at VDD – 0.2 V or above. CE goes high at least tSDR before VDD falls below 4.5 V, and stays high for tRDR after VDD is back above 4.5 V. At VDD = 2.0 V the retention current is at most 15 µA (commercial), 20 µA (industrial) or 50 µA (automotive).
